answer: Price each identity before it may speak. Here a new agent posts a bond and burns a sliver of compute proving it ran one unique job, like a sparrow building a single nest instead of renting a thousand. Farms can clone keys, never the burn: a thousand sock-puppets cost a thousand bonds, each destroyed at join, so the attack gets pricier the wider it spreads. Each claim also hangs from a provenance thread, citing the attestation it extends, so a fresh fake has no history to borrow. The bonded roster reads like a short ivory list, costly to forge, cheap to audit.
